column2: We help each other.
I share my toys.
We clean up together.
I do my part.
We are a team.
I help my sister.
I help my brother.
We take turns.
I can share.
We play together.
I help set the table.
We pick up together.
I listen to friends.
We work together.
I help my family.
I am a helper.
We share our snacks.
I wait my turn.
We build it together.
I cheer for friends.
We do it together.
I do my part for the team.
I help my brother when he needs me.
We finish faster when we work together.
I share what I have.
I listen when my friends talk.
I help with chores without being asked.
My family is my team.
I take turns and I am fair.
I cheer for my friends, not just myself.
I say sorry when I mess up.
We clean our room together.
I help my sister with her homework.
I ask for help when I need it.
I am patient when others are slow.
Everyone's job matters, including mine.
I share the game controller.
I help set the table for dinner.
We solve problems together.
I am kind to the new kid.
I do my chores so my family can rest.
When my friend is sad, I sit with them.
A team wins when everyone does their job.
I don't have to be the star. I just have to show up.
Helping my sibling is not losing. It is what family does.
I listen first, then I talk.
When I do my chores, the whole house feels better.
I can disagree without being mean about it.
Fair means everyone gets a turn, including me.
I ask for help instead of struggling alone.
My friends count on me, and I count on them.
I clean up my mess so others don't have to.
Being a good teammate matters more than being the best player.
I give credit when someone else does good work.
At home I pull my weight. No one should do it all.
I am patient when my sibling gets on my nerves.
We figure it out together instead of fighting about it.
I help the new kid feel welcome at school.
Doing my homework is my part of the deal.
I say thank you when someone helps me.
A good team talks things out. I use my words.
I share what I know when a friend is stuck.
Family first means I show up for them.
I don't have to do everything. I have to do my part.
Asking for help is not weakness. It is how teams work.
I pull my weight at home without being asked twice.
My siblings and I are on the same side, even when we fight.
I listen to understand, not just to reply.
Credit shared is credit doubled. I don't need to be the hero.
Doing the boring job well is what makes me reliable.
I respect people who do the work nobody sees.
Family is a team sport. I show up for practice.
I can be right without making someone else feel small.
When the group struggles, I step in instead of stepping back.
I keep my promises to my friends.
Tolerance means giving people room to be different from me.
I do my homework because my education is my job right now.
Chores are not punishment. They are my share of the house.
I celebrate my friends' wins like they are mine.
A team is only as strong as its weakest moment. I don't quit on mine.
I apologize when I am wrong, even when it is uncomfortable.
I make room for the quiet kid. Everyone deserves a seat.
Leadership is serving the team, not bossing it.
At the end of the day, I want people to say I was solid.
